items.q: And there was this lead trumpet player, Nick, he had the most beautiful sound.

ctx.x: I mean the first two sound like some old black man doing his blues. And you can see in their faces they’re blown away. So I mean early on, it’s been twenty years probably, since that started. I saw there is a way to really find ways to get the sound out. Like I sing in the car [scats] you can learn that. And there’s nothing wrong with making new language. But finding your inner voice. So it’s really been a blessing and a gift to me. Like I go into a room and I’ve been doing a lot of stuff at Lincoln Center, not…

techniques. I mean and it’s just about getting them to get a sound. I remember one time I was at UVA uh, the Commonwealth, with Doug Richards, a great teacher down there, he had me there for a week. And there was this lead trumpet player, Nick, he had the most beautiful sound. But there was nothing inside the sound, it was just beautiful. Physically you learn how to do it. And just ideas would come to me, like these movement ideas and stuff, leaning the stomach against the hand, and all kinds of stuff. So a…
